# HCheckbox

> A native checkbox with a mixed-state option and optional description.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HCheckbox` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-checkbox>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthCheckboxElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HCheckbox.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The model is boolean. The value prop is the submitted string for a checked checkbox; unchecked checkboxes contribute no form entry.
- indeterminate is a mixed visual state, not a third form value. Handle update:indeterminate(false) after user interaction, or use v-model:indeterminate.

## Public API

label, description, name, value: string · modelValue, checked, indeterminate, required, disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: boolean;
    checked?: boolean;
    indeterminate?: boolean;
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    name?: string;
    value?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
    required?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ modelValue: undefined, checked: false, value: "on" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(checked), update:indeterminate(false), change(checked)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: boolean
    ];
    "update:indeterminate": [
        value: boolean
    ];
    change: [
        value: boolean
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, control, label, description

Use `hearth-checkbox::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HCheckbox } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const enabled = ref(true);
</script>

<template>
  <HCheckbox v-model="enabled" label="Email summaries" name="summaries" value="yes" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-checkbox');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Email summaries",
  "name": "summaries",
  "value": "yes",
  "checked": true
});
element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});
mount.append(element);
```
